clue.text: Nervous tension as maladministered pension claimed by workers

indicators.note: something claimed by workers is held between them, so the shuffled letters sit inside

parts.note: worker ants, here used twice, one lot on each side

indicators.note: a badly run pension has its letters mismanaged, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A worker feels stress because the union's pension scheme has been badly run and must be fought for.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Workers' gives ANTS twice, one on each side of INONESP, the anagram of PENSION; 'as' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To have ants in your pants is an idiom for being restless and agitated, so it describes jittery nervous tension.

clue.text: Uncensored photo catching face of lothario in withdrawal

indicators.note: the photo-and-letter group goes in the middle of the withdrawal word

parts.note: an exit is a withdrawal or departure

indicators.note: the photo word catches, that is holds inside, the single letter

parts.note: pic is short for picture, a photo

indicators.note: the face of a word is its front, so its first letter

parts.note: a lothario is a seducer; only the first letter is wanted

explanation.surface: A racy picture catches a womaniser in the act of pulling out.
explanation.definitionFit: Explicit material is shown in full graphic detail, which is what uncensored content is.

clue.text: Ultimate in disappointment, wife getting diamonds another time

indicators.note: the ultimate letter in a word is its last one

parts.note: ice is slang for diamonds

explanation.surface: After a letdown, a husband gives his wife diamonds to try again.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something twice means doing it once more, a second occasion, beyond the first.

clue.text: Discover advantage in fruit like a peach, shortly

indicators.note: the advantage word sits in the middle of the shortened fruit
cut short, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: a drupe is a stone fruit such as a peach or plum
an edge is an advantage

explanation.surface: Someone discovers that a peach-like fruit gives them an advantage.
explanation.definitionFit: To dredge up is to unearth or bring to light something long buried or forgotten.

clue.text: Same thing lacking heart penned by sovereign journo

indicators.note: penned means enclosed, so the shortened word goes inside the sovereign's letters

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, stands for the sovereign

indicators.note: the central letter of the word is taken away

parts.note: ditto means the same thing again

explanation.surface: A newspaper writer, scorned by the monarch, keeps repeating the same heartless line.
explanation.definitionFit: A journo is a journalist, and an editor is a senior journalist who runs a publication.

clue.text: 20 22: up for something sweet?

indicators.note: the cross-reference 20 begins with rum, meaning odd or strange, which signals that the letters are jumbled

parts.note: with rum serving as the signal, the rest of the drink named at 20 and 22 is the fodder
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone is in the mood for a rum and Coke, keen on a sweet treat.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the cross-reference as RUM AND COKE: 'rum' (odd, strange) is the anagram signal, so it does two jobs, and AND, COKE and UP are the letters it rearranges; 'for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Pound cake is a rich sponge, named for its pound each of butter, sugar, eggs and flour, so a sweet dessert.

clue.text: Island boasting a vehicle, out of bounds

indicators.note: the bounds of the phrase are its outermost letters, which are cast out

parts.note: boasting can mean having or featuring, as in with
a car is a vehicle

explanation.surface: An island proudly has a car, but it's a restricted area.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove the first and last letters of WITHACAR.
explanation.definitionFit: Ithaca is the Greek island ruled by Odysseus, his home in Homer's epic.

clue.text: This contract's unconditional: these two setters must be appreciated!

definitions.text: This contract's unconditional: these two setters must be appreciated!

parts.words: This contract's unconditional: these two setters must be appreciated!
parts.note: the clue writer refers to himself in the first person, and a setter is also a breed of dog; love means appreciate, applied to each of the two

explanation.surface: The setter demands appreciation for himself and his dog under an unconditional deal.
explanation.walkthrough: The two setters are Paul, the setter who wrote the clue, and a gundog of the setter breed; each must be loved, and the proverb makes the deal all-or-nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverb asks that if you accept a person, you accept everything that comes with them, with no conditions.

clue.text: Heaven observed: head turns when this happens, by the sound of it?

indicators.note: the phrase is heard rather than written, so it sounds like the answer

parts.words: observed: head turns when this happens
parts.note: the head turns when the neck's twirled, said aloud

explanation.surface: A head-turning sight of heaven, observed with a sense of wonder.
explanation.walkthrough: When the neck's twirled, the head turns; said aloud, that phrase gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The next world is the afterlife, a common euphemism for paradise after death.

clue.text: Better off, con

parts.note: out means off, as in lights out
to do someone is to con or swindle them

explanation.surface: A conman who is better off than he was.
explanation.definitionFit: To outdo someone is to surpass them, which is what better means as a verb.

clue.text: Stopping cut, power connected

indicators.note: something stopping a word plugs a gap in it, so the letter goes inside

parts.note: sliced means cut
P is the physics symbol for power

explanation.surface: A cable is cut, stopping the supply until the power is reconnected.
explanation.definitionFit: Spliced ropes or wires are joined end to end, so they are linked together.

clue.text: Duty put Harry in mood

indicators.note: the harrying word goes inside the mood word

parts.note: a tone is a mood, as in the tone of a meeting
to harry is to nag or pester

explanation.surface: A dutiful person is harassed into a bad mood.
explanation.definitionFit: Tonnage was historically a tax or duty levied on cargo by the ton.

clue.text: Appropriate condition

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to appropriate is to steal

explanation.walkthrough: Both senses are British slang: to nick is to steal, and in good nick means in good shape.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb sense means taking something illicitly, while the noun sense describes the state an object is in.

clue.text: Faltering trade, piece lower in value

indicators.note: faltering trade is unsteady, so its letters are shaken into a new order

explanation.surface: As commerce stumbles, a valuable item loses its worth.
explanation.definitionFit: To depreciate is to decrease in worth over time, as cars and machinery do.

clue.text: 20 22, island beverage primarily: something restorative about it

indicators.note: the restorative word goes about, that is around, the island and letter

parts.note: a cure is something restorative
Bali is an Indonesian island

indicators.note: primarily means the first letter only

parts.note: only its first letter is used

explanation.surface: An island's drink is, first of all, a tonic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it' refers back to the island-and-letter group the cure goes about.
explanation.definitionFit: A Cuba libre is the cocktail of rum and cola with lime, so it names the drink at 20 and 22.

clue.text: Bid cut after review of great deal

indicators.note: the cut of meat comes after the reversed word
a review looks back, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: a ton is a great deal, as in tons of
rump is a cut of beef

explanation.surface: A trade negotiation is reduced after a big agreement is reassessed.
explanation.definitionFit: In bridge a no-trump call is a bid to play a hand without any trump suit.

clue.text: Grabbing new desk, old chairman manages

indicators.note: grabbing means holding, so the shuffled letters go inside

parts.note: Mao Zedong was Chairman of the Chinese Communist Party

indicators.note: renewing a word makes it in a new arrangement, so the letters are reordered

explanation.surface: An elderly boss seizes a new desk and gets by.
explanation.definitionFit: To make do is to cope with what is available, just as one manages or gets by.

clue.text: Piece provided, worn pipe

parts.note: a man is a piece in chess or draughts
if means provided, as in provided that
old means worn

explanation.surface: A worn pipe is supplied as a spare part.
explanation.definitionFit: A manifold is a pipe or chamber with several openings, as in an engine's exhaust system.

clue.text: Fare-dodger observed commandeering tug, certainly

indicators.note: commandeering means taking over, so the word takes the tug word inside

parts.note: saw means observed
to tow is to tug
ay means yes, certainly

explanation.surface: A passenger dodging payment is seen hijacking a tugboat.
explanation.definitionFit: A stowaway hides aboard a ship or plane to travel without paying.

clue.text: Better than America looking back, group embracing success

indicators.note: looking back means the word is read backwards

parts.note: US is the abbreviation for the United States

indicators.note: the group word embraces, holding inside, the success word

parts.note: a ring is a group, such as a gang
a pass is a success in an exam

explanation.surface: An America in retreat whose group surrounds success.
explanation.definitionFit: Surpassing as an adjective means exceeding, superior to or outdoing others.

clue.text: Alcoholic drink with mother: surprisingly uncorked bottles!

indicators.note: bottles means holds inside, so the mother word goes in the shuffled letters
the word comes out surprisingly, in an unexpected order

parts.note: taken as written
ma is mother

explanation.surface: Mother is shocked to find bottles uncorked and spirits mixed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bottles' looks like a noun for the drink containers, but it is the verb that puts mother inside; 'with' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Rum and coke is a mixed drink of rum with cola.

clue.text: Battered cod has head of bream alongside

indicators.note: cod as an adjective means fake or mock, so the letters are rearranged
the head of a word is its first letter

parts.note: by means alongside, beside

explanation.surface: Battered fish served with a bream head beside it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cod' looks like a fish but it is the anagram signal; HAS rearranged gives SHA.
explanation.definitionFit: Something shabby is worn out and in poor condition, like a battered old coat.

clue.text: See 20
Sailing boat in small puddles, capsized

indicators.note: capsized means turned over, so the down word is read upside down

parts.note: pools are small bodies of water, like puddles

explanation.surface: A boat sitting in shallow puddles has overturned.
explanation.definitionFit: A sloop is a one-masted sailing vessel with a fore-and-aft rig.

clue.text: Every one detailed, I made plays for the theatre

indicators.note: detailed means losing its tail, the last letter

parts.note: all means every one

indicators.note: plays means messes about, so the letters move into a new order

explanation.surface: Everyone is described in detail in the plays I wrote for the stage.
explanation.walkthrough: I MADE rearranged gives MEIDA; 'for' is a link. The Almeida is a theatre in Islington, London.
explanation.definitionFit: The Almeida is a well-known London playhouse, so it is an example of a theatre.

clue.text: Error in emergency call, a firefighter sent the wrong way

indicators.note: sent the wrong way means the letters are taken backwards
the letters are inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: A mistake in an emergency call sends a firefighter to the wrong address.
explanation.walkthrough: Inside 'emergency call, a firefighter' sits YCALLAF; read backwards it gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A fallacy is a mistaken belief or faulty argument, a kind of mistake.

clue.text: Skilled listener: fish in one's ear?

indicators.note: heard in one's ear, the word is spoken, so it sounds like the answer

parts.note: tuna is a fish

explanation.surface: An expert listener asks whether there is a fish in their ear.
explanation.walkthrough: In a British accent, with no final r sound, tuna and the answer sound alike.
explanation.definitionFit: A piano tuner adjusts pitch by ear, so the job needs a finely trained listener.

clue.text: South American politician, or an old pig from the right

indicators.note: read from the right means the letters go backwards

parts.note: a pig is a slob, a messy person

explanation.surface: A Latin American leader called either a has-been or a pig.
explanation.definitionFit: Jair Bolsonaro was president of Brazil from 2019 to 2022.
